regulations.primary_reference: International Residential Code (IRC) for one- and two-family dwellings; International Building Code (IBC) for commercial. Adopted with amendments state-by-state.

residential_irc_r311_7.note: US uses imperial by default. State amendments may adjust — always verify local code.

commercial_ibc.note: Commercial IBC significantly stricter than residential IRC — do not conflate.

regulations.state_variance: California (CBC), New York City, Massachusetts, Florida all publish amended codes. Always check local building department.

cultural_preferences: Feature staircases in the entrance foyer are a US signature — the stair as first-impression object drives grander proportions than UK equivalents.
Curved and open-foyer staircases much more common than in UK due to larger homes.
Oak treads with painted risers is universal; wrought iron balusters are more common than in UK.
Carpet runners on stairs are still common in traditional and colonial styles.
Maple and cherry are US popular species alongside oak — walnut for luxury.

supplier_categories.big_box_retailers: Home Depot, Lowe's — general building supplies, some stair parts (limited premium range)
supplier_categories.stair_specialists: L.J. Smith Stair Systems, Fitts, StairSupplies.com, Stair Parts USA — dominant US stair-parts brands
supplier_categories.hardwood_lumber: Regional hardwood specialists — most metros have several
supplier_categories.stair_manufacturers: Regional bespoke shops; national kit suppliers like Salter Spiral Stair (spirals), Southern Staircase
supplier_categories.glass_balustrade: AGS Stainless, ACS Stainless, StairSupplies.com Prova Glass, Fortress Building Products
supplier_categories.finishing: Bona (floor-industry crossover), Watco, Waterlox, Rubio Monocoat US
supplier_categories.note: US supplier directory is not built in NEX yet — V2 target.

colonial_traditional.notes: Grand entrance foyer common. Wide staircases with curved bottom steps.

ranch_style.notes: Single-storey — no main staircase, sometimes basement access only.

modern_open_plan.notes: Floating and open-riser stairs increasingly popular. Cable and glass balustrades common.

loft_conversion_urban.notes: Industrial style dominates. Steel + oak combinations. NYC and Chicago drive the trend.

regulatory_warnings: US codes are STATE-specific with local amendments — never quote 'US code' without verifying the specific jurisdiction.
IRC residential and IBC commercial are different envelopes — get the building type right first.
California (CBC) has additional seismic and accessibility requirements.
New York City has extensive local amendments beyond the IBC.
Historic districts may have preservation requirements affecting stair modifications.
not_in_v1: Climate zone considerations (Florida humidity vs Arizona dry vs New England seasonal swing) for timber selection
